real_gaps: The 6-year post baccalaureate experience requirement is not a paperwork technicality here. Engineer IV reporting to a Lead Engineer II, with language like guidance only in controversial circumstances and lead or perform in engineering projects, describes a role assuming independent engineering judgment built over years, not academic-project judgment. Nothing in the profile substitutes for that.

Zero domain exposure to vehicles, chassis systems, or heavy equipment. All embedded work is robotics/arms/turrets at hobbyist or research scale. No CAN bus, no vehicle network protocols, nothing that signals familiarity with how software integrates into an actual machine chassis.

Formal system failure mode analysis and risk assessment (FMEA style, applying EE principles to predict system behavior under failure scenarios) is completely absent. This is not adjacent to anything in the profile. it is a distinct engineering discipline usually learned on the job in regulated/safety-conscious industries, and there is no proxy for it here.

The documentation this JD wants (compliance-grade design and test documentation to Engineering Standards) is a different rigor than the BOM/claims doc from the Planctech internship or JupyterHub notes from BARC. those are informal by comparison.
overstated_by_keywords: Real-time/Linux and schematics/PCB read as clean Have/Adjacent matches on keywords alone, but the underlying scale is single-board, single-developer, academic-project embedded systems. not a production vehicle ECU built to Engineering Standards with cross-team compliance. llm_analysis.reasoning: The technical vocabulary overlaps well (RTOS, Linux, C, PCB, oscilloscopes) which is why the keyword match came out at 80%.
